lines: FERRY TO CORVANE
No crossings while the lake is restless.
FERRY TO CORVANE
Crossings resume. Ferryman: Aldo.
The fish stopped jumping the night the Rift opened.
Even the reeds sound quieter. That's the Hush, they say.
Something glints on the reed islet west of the pier. Too far to wade, though.
Say, have you seen a Kelpup? The pups used to bark at my boat. Bring one by, would you?
That Kelpup of yours barked at my boat. Just like old times.
The fish are jumping again! Whole shoals of them, right by the pier.
That's your doing, I'd wager. The Rift's closed and the water's singing.
Tangled in the reeds: a Waking Moss!
Only reeds now, rustling in the wind.
My Puddlet won't answer when I call it anymore.
Grandpa Aldo says a Wayfarer with a strong bond can wake it up again.
Puddlet splashes me every morning now! Thank you, {name}!
Puddlet called for me all by itself this morning! Both Rifts are closed, aren't they?
Thank you, {name}! Puddlet says thank you too. Splash!
Crier: Hear ye! Veydal keeps its festivals, storm or no storm.
daily: Crier: Hear ye! The ferryman swears the lake was warm this morning. Nobody believes him.
Crier: Hear ye! Lost: one fishing hat. Found: one Kelpup wearing a fishing hat.
Crier: Hear ye! The lighthouse lamp burned all night again. Aldo says it always will.
Crier: Hear ye! Market day! Bring coin, bring baskets, leave your Spirlings' muddy paws outside.
Crier: Hear ye! Mind the reeds by the pier. Something hums in there at dusk.

lines: Wynn: Every week the lake throws up three new echoes. Same ones for every Wayfarer in Veydal.
Wynn: Beat all five and I'll pay out. Once a week, mind.
Ines: The lighthouse keeps old Rift echoes. I can wake them for you.
Ines: Five Wayfarers' echoes in a row, no rest in between. They grow with you.
Kestra: Two Rifts mended. The valley is calmer... and smaller.
Kestra: There's a third one, up north past the crest. Bigger than both.
Kestra: I still think something lives on the other side. When the ferry runs again, we find out together.
Kestra: So? Do we cross together?
Kestra: When Aldo opens the ferry, I'll be on it. Save me a seat.
Kestra: Going alone, then. I'll see you on the other side anyway.
Aldo waits by the boat, his old oar across his knees.
Aldo: Hold on tight. The lake still has opinions.
Aldo stops rowing and rubs his shoulder.

ferry_row_self: You take the oar. It's heavier than it looks.
Aldo: Ha! Mirela rowed like that. All arms, no rhythm. Keep going.
ferry_row_aldo: Aldo: Forty years since I rowed this far. Give an old man a minute.
He rows on, slow and steady, humming the lighthouse tune.
kestra_dock_together: Kestra: Good. Two cartographers see twice as much.
Kestra: I'll go ahead to Corvane once the ferry runs. Find me in Madderby.
kestra_dock_alone: Kestra: Hm. Your call. Mirela went alone too, you know.
Kestra: I'll still be in Corvane. Someone has to map what you mend.

lines: Can you sing to it? The way Wayfarers do?
You kneel by the little Puddlet and listen for its call...
The Puddlet blinks, then chirps back at you!
Puddlet is awake! Here, take this. I found it on the beach.

child_retry: The Puddlet stays quiet. Maybe try again in a moment.

lines: Tilda: Festival ribbons for festival goods! Ribbons turn into Waymarks when the festival ends, so nothing goes to waste.
A light rises from under the lake by the shore.
It hums a note you have heard before, in the lamp room, when Mirela's map book fell open.
The light takes shape. It is Velahra, the First Voice of Veydal. It was the last to see Mirela.
Here, take these. A fisher pays his debts.
Boatwoman Hedda: Lake Line! Reedhaven and Quillbrook, if you've been there on foot.
Driver Odo: Valley Coach. Thornridge, Copperfold, Wrenhollow. Only stops you know.
Netmender Brin: My nets have more holes than Wim's excuses, and I still catch more than he delivers.
Netmender Brin: The lake sings again since the Rift went quiet. The nets feel it too.
Baker Lotte: Wim's cart is so slow the bread goes stale on the way. I've started baking it stale. Saves time.
Baker Lotte: My dough rises properly again. The Rift must have been sitting on it.
Rower Tilda: I'd row Wim across the lake for free. Halfway. Then I'd row back.
Rower Tilda: The water's clear down to the stones again. You did that, didn't you?
Lamplighter Joss: I keep the lamp burning all night so Lotte can see how flat her bread is.
Lamplighter Joss: The lamp burns steady now. No more flicker from the east.
Carter Wim: Everybody laughs at my cart. Even the cart. It squeaks every time someone says my name.
Carter Wim: The road feels lighter since the Rift was sealed. Even the cart squeaks less.
An old cartographer's stone. A compass rose is cut into it, worn almost smooth.
Fishwife Marit: Market day! Dried kelp towels and cool gel, straight off the boats.

lines: Herbwoman Agnes: Brews from the fen, only on market days. Smell that.
Tinker Rasmus: Wednesday and Saturday, rain or shine. Charms and leaves, fair prices.
Carter Wim: Stop! Fine, take these coins, just stop squeaking about my cart.
